clue.text: Dog riding sheep

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog
riding a horse is being on it

explanation.surface: A dog perched on the back of a sheep, as at a country show.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutton is the meat of a mature sheep, so the word stands for the animal by extension.

clue.text: Something orbiting, orbiting a vehicle, takes the biscuit

indicators.note: orbiting means circling round, so the moon goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a moon is a body that orbits a planet
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A space-age image of satellites circling a craft, ending with the idiom for outdoing everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the' is link wording borrowed from the idiom 'takes the biscuit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroon is a small almond or coconut biscuit.

clue.text: Gate unhinged by forest refreshment area

indicators.note: unhinged means deranged, so the letters of the gate are thrown into a new order

parts.note: Arden is the forest of Shakespeare's As You Like It, once covering Warwickshire

explanation.surface: A gate knocked off its hinges by a woodland, beside a place for refreshments.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea garden is an outdoor cafe where refreshments are served.

clue.text: Fudge hot? A promise

indicators.note: to fudge is to fiddle or falsify, so these letters are tampered with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about hot fudge, followed by a promise, like a sweetshop pledge.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn promise or vow.

clue.text: Fellow consumer writing point in Panama?

indicators.note: in places the pen point inside the waterway

parts.note: the Panama Canal, signalled as an example by the question mark
a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: A shopper writing a note while at a point somewhere in Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow consumer' is a joke: one who consumes his fellows, a person who eats people.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannibal eats members of his own species, so is literally a consumer of his fellows.

clue.text: FC to goad? Reckless, unlikely event

indicators.note: reckless means wild and careless, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A football club being urged recklessly, as fans goad their team.
explanation.definitionFit: An act of God is an unforeseeable natural disaster, an event nobody could predict.

clue.text: To goad? Reckless, given irritating complaint

parts.note: to nettle someone is to goad or irritate them
rash means reckless or hasty

explanation.surface: Goading someone recklessly brings on an irritating complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Nettle rash, or hives, is an itchy skin condition, an irritating ailment.

clue.text: Instrument shown up in Simpson arrest

indicators.note: in a down entry, shown up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: O. J. Simpson, the American footballer and actor
to nab is to arrest

explanation.surface: A news line about an instrument revealed when O. J. Simpson was arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is a stringed musical instrument with a round drum-like body.

clue.text: Find dead duck about to be caught

indicators.note: the duck and about are caught, held inside the word for dead

parts.note: the late someone is someone who has died
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A hunter tries to find a dead duck that is about to be grabbed.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate something is to find where it is.

clue.text: Man carrying underwear initially, he had a slip

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside, so the man's name encloses the letter

parts.note: Fred is a man's name

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the word underwear

explanation.surface: A man with underwear, who had a slip: a mild comic sketch of a mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'slip' is a Freudian slip, a verbal error said to reveal the unconscious, and also plays on the undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: The psychoanalyst gave his name to the Freudian slip, so he is the man behind that kind of mistake.

clue.text: Vessel under vessel?

definitions.meaning: a ship that trades along the shoreline
a small mat placed beneath a glass or cup

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a ship sailing along the coast; the other is a drinks mat that sits under a glass.

clue.text: Some giant (it an iceberg)

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the letters run within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A remark that part of a giant was hit by an iceberg.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the giant liner, sunk by an iceberg.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant ocean liner famously struck an iceberg in 1912 and sank.

clue.text: Become rampant observing bottom

definitions.meaning: to rise on the hind legs, as a heraldic rampant lion

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to rise up on hind legs like a horse; the other is the backside.

clue.text: Shabby, then locate different garment

parts.note: duff is slang for poor or useless

indicators.note: different means altered, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something shabby, then an attempt to find a different garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A duffel coat is a hooded woollen coat fastened with toggles.

clue.text: Am I not able to force open the bridge?

parts.note: can't I is the same as am I not able
to lever is to prise or force open

explanation.surface: A plaintive question about prising open a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a type of bridge built on projecting beams supported at one end.

clue.text: Experience two poorish grades in exam

indicators.note: in places the grades inside the exam

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam
D and E are low exam grades

explanation.surface: A student's account of getting two poor marks in an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful or harrowing experience.

clue.text: Friend and artist with 500 income?

annotationWithheld.why: Friend and artist with 500 income? (7): the parse puts RA + D in COME, with 'income' read as 'come' and 'in' at once, one word doing two jobs (container indicator and fodder).

clue.text: Where many nod off at dim or stupid politician

indicators.note: stupid here means muddled, so the letters of the words are jumbled

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Many people dozing off at a dim, stupid politician's speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormitory is a large room where many people sleep.

clue.text: Not fit to see the little demon exposed

parts.note: an imp is a small demon
aired means exposed to the open air or made public

explanation.surface: The little demon has been exposed and is now too unfit to be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaired means damaged or weakened, so not in good working order.

clue.text: Invention of Nobel which could end amity?

indicators.note: could suggests what the letters might become when reworked into another order

explanation.surface: A remark that Nobel's invention could end friendship between nations.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Nobel invented the explosive and endowed the Nobel Peace Prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel patented the explosive in 1867, his most famous invention.

clue.text: Bodily structure an elementary thing with male chromosome

parts.note: an atom is the smallest unit of an element
Y is the chromosome that marks a male

explanation.surface: A biology lesson linking body shape, atoms and the male chromosome.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy is the bodily structure of a creature, studied in medicine.

clue.text: Outsize catch for fish-eating bird

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
prey is what a hunter catches

explanation.surface: A large haul of fish caught for a seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a hawk that dives to catch fish.

clue.text: Pass, otherwise a copper collected

indicators.note: collected means gathered up, so the other pieces are held inside the word for otherwise

parts.note: else means otherwise
P stands for a penny, a copper coin

explanation.surface: Otherwise, a policeman picked up the pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is a penny coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Time elapses when it passes by.

clue.text: Try dash of tequila for spirit

parts.note: a judge tries or hears a case

indicators.note: a dash of means just a little, so the first letter of the drink

explanation.surface: An invitation to try a drop of tequila for some spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests drink, but it means courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart, like spirit, means courage or enthusiasm.

clue.text: Unprofitable product sees dollar collapsing

indicators.note: collapsing means falling apart, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A firm watches the dollar fall and finds its product has become unprofitable.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss leader is an item sold below cost to draw shoppers in.

clue.text: Reliable, therefore on top

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: so means therefore
a lid is a top or cover

explanation.surface: Something is reliable, therefore it comes out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid means dependable and sound, like a trustworthy person.

clue.text: Five is answer? Pass

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A quiz moment: is five the answer, or should I pass?
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official pass allowing entry to a country.

clue.text: Deliveries completed

definitions.meaning: in cricket a set of six balls bowled from one end

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a set of six balls bowled from one end; also a word for finished.

clue.text: Friend has to declare it's blarney

parts.note: a pal is a friend
to aver is to declare or assert

explanation.surface: A friend must declare that it's all smooth talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Palaver is long-winded idle talk, much like blarney or flattery.

clue.text: Italian food managed with something stringy, both short of names

indicators.note: both pieces lose a letter standing for name, so each drops its N

parts.note: ran means managed, as running a business
a violin is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Italian cooking done alongside something stringy, both lacking names.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the standard abbreviation for name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small square pasta parcels, a classic Italian dish.

clue.text: Terribly dear London, no news of city paved with gold

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters are badly jumbled
no means the letters for news are left out of the rearranged words

parts.note: news read as plural Ns, N being short for new

explanation.surface: A lament that dear old London has terribly little news.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping both Ns from DEAR LONDON leaves eight letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado was the legendary South American city of gold sought by explorers.

clue.text: Sock pattern where layering out, not in

indicators.note: out signals the letters are rearranged
not means the letters of the little word are left out

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tip on knitting a sock pattern where layering is left out, not in.
explanation.definitionFit: Argyle is a knitted diamond pattern, classic on socks and sweaters.
